rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding nanoscale dispersoid particles (carbides/oxides), whereas the paper compared a Re-containing alloy with a Re-free alloy under He-ion irradiation. These are different kinds of interventions (compositional addition vs. dispersoid incorporation), so the hypothesis does not reconstruct the paper's intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature (>800°C) and reactor-like irradiation, while the paper used room-temperature deposition, room-temperature 120 keV He2+ irradiation, and room-temperature nanoindentation/compression. These are different regimes, so the hypothesis does not agree with the paper's conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes dispersion strengthening via particle pinning of dislocations and grain boundaries, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on defect-sink sites (grain boundaries, lattice distortion, amorphous regions) from Re addition to suppress He-bubble growth and embrittlement. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased yield strength and creep resistance at high temperatures with similar stability, while the paper measured reduced irradiation hardening and embrittlement at room temperature. The predicted property (high-temperature strength/creep) and direction differ from the paper's outcome (room-temperature irradiation resistance).
